Yes—almost certainly.

A **28% illuminated waxing crescent**, **44.5° above the horizon**, and **64° from the Sun** is not a marginal naked-eye target. Even during civil twilight, with clear skies and knowing roughly where to look, an ordinary observer should be able to see it readily. Its southwesterly position also puts it well away from the brightest part of the twilight sky near the Sun in the west-northwest.

Clouds, buildings, or unusually poor transparency could hide it, but under the conditions you specified, the Moon would **not** be impossible to see.
